items.answer: Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team, not by the individual, to ensure team onsite days overlap and office time is collaborative. The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average in MosaicOne rather than week by week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem. A week containing a company holiday, approved PTO or approved travel reduces the requirement proportionally.

Next steps:
- Confirm your team's specific onsite days with your manager, typically Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

Basic life insurance and accidental death and dismemberment cover begin when the medical waiting period ends.

The 401(k) retirement plan has no waiting period; employees may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

The waiting period is not restarted by an internal transfer, promotion, or change from part-time to full-time status, but is restarted by a break in service of more than 26 weeks.

Benefits enrollment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends, so elections are in place when eligibility arrives.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate your exact coverage start date
- Enroll in benefits during week one of onboarding to ensure elections are ready when the waiting period ends
- Contact People Operations with questions about your specific coverage timeline

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

If a message arrives asking you to send sensitive data to an external address, do not reply and do not act on the request; report it to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example and delete it.

Recommendation — not company policy: Treat this as a suspected phishing attempt. The combination of urgency, a request for bulk data, and an external address are classic phishing signals. Forward the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example so the security team can investigate and track the threat.

Next steps:
- Forward the email to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Delete the message
- Do not reply to the sender
- Do not send any data

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories. The allowance is intended for items such as a desk, chair, lamp, footrest, adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, and small filing cabinet.

The allowance resets on 1 January and does not carry over. It is available to hybrid and fully remote employees; onsite employees may claim against it only where their manager has agreed a regular remote pattern in MosaicOne.

Laptops, monitors, docks, keyboards, mice, headsets and webcams are not claimed against this allowance; they are issued as company assets under the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Items purchased under the allowance belong to the employee and are not returned at separation. The allowance is taxable in some jurisdictions; MosaicOne applies the correct treatment automatically for each entity.

Next steps:
- Review the Equipment & Asset Policy for items issued as company assets
- Confirm your employment status (hybrid, fully remote, or onsite with manager approval) in MosaicOne to verify eligibility

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent. The 16 weeks are the same whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Confirm your eligibility (6 months of continuous service required)
- Contact People Operations to discuss timing and whether you wish to split the leave into up to three blocks of at least two weeks each

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met — a remote field site with one hotel, a sold-out market — the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed; the note is enough.

Next steps:
- Review the approved-city list and conference dates to confirm which cap applies to your destination
- Submit your lodging expense in MosaicOne Expenses with a note if you exceed the cap due to unavailability

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins. The review determines whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request is raised in MosaicOne alongside the manager approval and names the destination, the exact dates, the workspace address and a short description of the work the employee will perform while abroad.

A trip that exceeds 30 consecutive days requires director approval rather than direct-manager approval. Manager approval, director approval and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

The employee must hold the right to work in the destination country, must meet the device and connectivity requirements, and must stay inside the company's rolling 90-day annual limit.

Employees must have completed at least 12 months of continuous service to work outside their home country.

Next steps:
- Submit Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne at least 21 calendar days before departure
- Obtain director approval (not just manager approval)
- Provide destination, exact dates, workspace address, and work description to Tax & Legal
- Confirm eligibility: 12+ months tenure, good standing, right to work in destination country

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees. The cap covers the room rate only; local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above it.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

For an expense report of USD 2,501 to USD 10,000, the approver is the Director with Finance business partner review.

Every trip needs manager approval before booking. Trips involving more than four travellers from the same team, or trips with a total estimated cost above USD 10,000, additionally require director approval.

Next steps:
- Submit the conference trip through MosaicOne Travel with manager approval before booking
- Ensure flight booking occurs at least 14 calendar days before departure
- Retain itemised receipts for all expenses of USD 25 or more
- Route the USD 3,000 expense report to your director for approval with Finance business partner review

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date. It is the only training with a hard deadline shorter than 30 days, because system access is granted on day one and the risk starts with it.

The full required set for every employee is: security and acceptable use, data protection and privacy, anti-harassment and respectful workplace, and anti-bribery and corruption. All four are completed within 30 calendar days of the start date.

Benefits enrolment opens in week one even though coverage does not begin until the 90-day waiting period ends. Enrolling early means the elections are in place when eligibility arrives.

Payroll setup, tax withholding elections and 401(k) enrolment are completed in week one. The 401(k) has no waiting period, so a new hire may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

IT ships standard equipment to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date. The shipment goes to the employee's home address for remote and hybrid hires and to their assigned office for onsite hires, and it contains the laptop, adapter, headset and, for remote hires, the monitor, keyboard, mouse and dock described in the Equipment & Asset Policy.

Every employee is issued a standard laptop configured for their role, a power adapter, a headset and a laptop bag. The standard configurations for 2026 are a 14-inch developer laptop with 32 GB of memory for engineering roles, and a 13-inch laptop with 16 GB of memory for all other roles.

Recommendation — not company policy: Engineering hires should clone the relevant repositories, build the codebase or bring up a bench, and land a first small change by the end of week one to prove that access, tooling and review all work.

Next steps:
- Confirm your start date and work location (remote, hybrid, or onsite) with your hiring manager so equipment ships to the correct address
- Complete identity verification, MosaicOne account activation, and multi-factor authentication on day one
- Attend the benefits question session (held every second Tuesday) in week one to understand your coverage options
- Complete all four required training modules by day 30: security and acceptable use (by day 14), data protection and privacy, anti-harassment and respectful workplace, and anti-bribery and corruption

People Operations acknowledges every reported concern within 2 business days. The acknowledgement names the person who will handle the case, explains the process, and sets out what the reporter can expect to be told and when.

Investigations are targeted for completion within 30 calendar days of the report. Where an investigation will take longer, the reporter and the respondent are both told, in writing, why and when to expect the outcome.

Severity 1 cases cover immediate risk to a person: violence or a threat of it, a safety incident with injury, a credible risk of self-harm, sexual misconduct involving physical contact, and any matter where someone must be separated from a situation today. Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours.

Target resolution times are as fast as the facts allow for Severity 1. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update. Updates continue at least every 10 business days until the case closes.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations at people-ops@mosaicrobotics.example or Employee Relations at employee-relations@mosaicrobotics.example to raise a workplace conduct concern
- Reference your case number in all follow-up communications to track progress

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

Unforeseeable absences—a sudden illness, a family emergency, a transport failure that makes work impossible—are never held to the notice requirement. The employee notifies their manager as early as they reasonably can, and the absence is entered in MosaicOne retroactively.

Your manager must answer your PTO request within three business days so that you can book travel, and must approve it unless there is a concrete business reason to deny it.

Next steps:
- Submit your PTO request in MosaicOne at least 5 business days (or 15 business days for 6+ consecutive days) before your first day of absence
- Your manager will respond within three business days
